A1.justification: Both PDFs describe WAVE, with matching authors, core methodology, and benchmark experiments. Text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison. The supplied v1 ends with references despite mentioning an appendix; v3 includes Appendices A–E, which were included in this assessment.

before.justification: V1 reports original ImageNet initialization experiments, evaluations on seven downstream datasets, and a component ablation in Tables 1–4.

after.justification: V3 retains original benchmark results and adds template sensitivity, ancestor-model and deeper-model experiments, learning curves, and weight and attention visualizations.

M1.justification: The shared templates, Kronecker reconstruction, distillation, and scaler fitting with frozen templates remain. However, v1 explicitly initializes target scalers randomly, whereas v3 Appendix B specifies linear-padding initialization using depth-dependent coefficients and small Gaussian noise. This changes a bounded initialization step.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet-1K and the same seven downstream image-classification datasets: Flowers, CUB, Cars, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Food-101, and iNaturalist-2019. Added model depths, ancestor architectures, and training analyses change configurations and procedures, rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Weight Selection is removed from the depth comparison in Table 1, while remaining in the width and downstream comparisons. Other principal comparators remain: Heru-LG/Heur-LG and TELG/TLEG are renamed versions of the same methods. Direct pretraining remains evaluated in v3 Figure 3.

E3.justification: V3 adds substantial experimental configurations: 24- and 36-layer targets, RegNet-16GF as an alternative ancestor, controlled template-count and shape variations, and 300-epoch WAVE-versus-scratch trajectories. The original 150-epoch template learning and 10-epoch initialization evaluations remain. Appendix C mainly discloses previously unspecified settings, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The original component ablation is retained as v3 Table 5. V3 additionally examines template count and shape, initialization-rule parameter costs, sensitivity to the ancestor model, convergence, weight correlations, and CAM localization. These substantially extend the questions investigated beyond v1's component-level analysis.

E5.justification: Neither PDF specifies repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or a defined statistical significance analysis. The additional tables and learning curves do not introduce an identifiable uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: WAVE's accuracies in Tables 1–3 are retained, but v3 adds substantial sensitivity, deeper-model, ancestor-model, and trajectory results. Small corrections include Heur-LG's DeiT-Ti L6 accuracy, 47.3 to 47.4, and the Table 2 W576 improvement, 3.6 to 3.9. Some direct-pretraining references also change: DeiT-Ti L12 is 68.6 in v1 Table 1 but 64.4 for 150-epoch scratch training in v3 Figure E.1, without an explained setting change.

T1.justification: V1 provides construction and loss equations but no formal proposition. V3 Appendix A adds Proposition 1 and a constructive proof presenting Heur-LG, Auto-LG, and TLEG as special cases of WAVE. The main formulation also corrects the distinction between attention outputs and QKV parameter matrices.

C1.justification: The central shared-template method, initialization benchmark, and superior-transfer claims remain. Quantified efficiency claims change materially within that retained contribution: the introduction replaces approximately n-fold computational savings with 15n-fold savings and changes the transferred-parameter headline from 16% to 3.3%, explicitly referencing the ancestry model in v3.

C2.justification: V3 adds substantive interpretations linking template capacity and shape to knowledge preservation, weight visualizations to automatically learned structure, and CAM localization to reduced background attention. Appendices D and E additionally interpret ancestor-model stability and rapid learning through size-agnostic knowledge and 'instincts.' These explanations substantially extend v1's component and transfer discussions.

D1.justification: V3 supplies the previously unavailable appendix details: optimization pseudocode, scaler initialization, auxiliary-model specifications, template counts, dataset splits, and extensive optimizer, augmentation, learning-rate, batch-size, and training-schedule tables. It also names a planned code repository. This improves documented reproducibility; the PDFs do not establish that the promised code is available.

R1.justification: V3 adds discussion or citations for KIND, FINE, learnable-transformation learngenes, Cluster-Learngene, and Net2Net, among others. It also explicitly positions earlier layer-based learngenes as special cases. The principal positioning against direct initialization, weight transformation, and layer-based inheritance remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, methods, and results are extensively rewritten and reorganized. V3 introduces numbered sections, separates preliminaries from template construction, renames knowledge condensation/decompression as integration/initialization, and creates dedicated direct-pretraining and visualization sections. This is substantial narrative revision beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: V3 redraws Figure 2, revises Figure 1, and reformats benchmark tables with parameter-count rows and highlighting. The tabular direct-pretraining comparison becomes Figure 3 with additional plots. New analysis tables, weight and CAM visualizations, appendix tables, and learning-curve grids substantially expand and reorganize the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: V3 is more reproducible and easier to evaluate because it supplies missing implementation details and controlled template and ancestor analyses. These gains are tempered by weaknesses in strengthened headline comparisons: the 150-epoch DeiT-Ti L12 reference changes from 68.6 to 64.4 without explanation, and 15n-fold savings do not follow from the stated 150-epoch preparation plus 10 epochs per target versus 150 epochs per independently trained target. The net improvement is therefore limited.
